ontology: Counterparties, legal entities, positions and SEC filings.
Any organisation identified by a CIK, LEI or both. Root of the entity hierarchy.
A legal entity that appears on at least one side of a trade or position.
A legal entity that issues securities held in positions.
An institutional investment manager or fund that reports holdings (13F filer).
A legal entity listed as a subsidiary in an Exhibit 21 style disclosure.
A holding of an instrument by a fund as of a reporting date.
A position change recorded as a discrete transaction.
A security identified by ticker, CUSIP or class (e.g. common stock, put, call).
An SEC filing (10-K, 13F-HR, ...) that is the provenance of triples.
Points from a subsidiary to its direct parent. Declared transitive so Stardog reasoning can materialise the closure; the API uses property paths so it works without reasoning.

Fraction of this entity owned by the parent it is a tg:subsidiaryOf, as disclosed in an Exhibit 21 style list. An entity has at most one parent in this dataset, so the fraction sits on the subsidiary instead of on a reified edge.
True when the disclosure carried no percentage and tg:ownershipFraction defaulted to 1.0.
Two counterparties that face each other through at least one position.
Denormalised shortcut from a position to the issuer of its instrument.
Market value in USD as reported.
One of COMMON, PREFERRED, DEBT, PUT, CALL.
Links a position or a subsidiary assertion to the filing it was extracted from.
SEC Central Index Key, zero padded to ten digits.

queries.periods:
# Reporting periods present in the store, newest first.
SELECT DISTINCT ?period
WHERE { ?pos tg:asOf ?period }
ORDER BY DESC(?period)
